pieces.text: is information that tells you something happened.

content.text: How do you look for evidence of a change to Earth's surface?

elements.text: There are many ways to find evidence of a change to Earth's surface. One way is to look at a picture that was taken after the change.

contents.text: Here are some examples of what the evidence for different changes might be:

elements.text: cracks in the ground
houses with broken walls and roofs
melted rock on Earth's surface
smoke coming out of a hole in the ground
a canyon with a river flowing through it
a river carrying sand and mud

content.text: Be careful when you are looking for evidence!

elements.text: A picture of Earth's surface can contain a lot of information. Some of that information might be evidence of a change to the surface, but some of it is not!

contents.text: For example, a picture taken after an earthquake might show a blue sky. But the color of the sky is not evidence of an earthquake. So, that information is not evidence that an earthquake happened.
